body:
Ok, I'll go into more detail on everything.
Didn't think one line change can cause that much confusion.


**Regarding completion and auto-insertion:**

> I don't really understand what you mean with the auto insertion part

There are essentially two types of completion behavior.

1\)
- Completion gets triggered, a completion menu appears
- Cycle through the menu to find the desired item
- Press enter to accept
- The completed item will be inserted into the text

2\)
- Completion gets triggered, a completion menu appears
- Cycle through the menu to find the desired item
- Each selected item gets inserted into the text immediately
- Cycling to the next item replaces the previously inserted text respectively
- When done, the user just continues writing, no need to accept or anything

When talking about auto-insertion, I'm referring to 2).

The [blink.cmp docs](https://cmp.saghen.dev/configuration/completion.html#list) have some demo videos for different completion behaviors.
Method 1) would correspond to `Manual` and 2) to `Manual, Auto Insert`.

I was *guessing* that this issue might prominently appear in editors with auto-insertion, but it is a more general bug actually, as I will explain further down.

Different editors may have different ways of communicating with the LSP server.
I'm not an LSP expert, so I don't know how editors implement different completion methods and corresponding LSP requests.
I'm also not a vscode user, so I don't know how completion works there.


**Regarding issue description and reproduction steps**

The issue is very similar to https://github.com/godotengine/godot-vscode-plugin/issues/842 but more consistent, apparently.

When cycling through completions, the LSP server returns empty documentation for functions.
Constants and members seem to work fine.
IIRC the `completionItem/resolve` handler goes down a completely different code path for resolving functions than for variables.

Using a slightly modified version of your example snippet.
Cursor position is marked with `|`.

```gdscript
extends Node2D

func test() -> void:
    var s: String
    s.|
```

- Move cursor after the dot and trigger completion
- The first completion item is `casecmp_to()`
- Selecting the completion shows an empty documentation popup


**Regarding #105236:**

I looked at the issue and while it sounds similar, it seems to be unrelated.
Even with #105236 applied, the same issue still appears.

I also ensured a fresh start of Godot before each test, but the same issue still exists.


**Regarding setup:**

- Neovim + `nvim-lspconfig` + `blink.cmp`
- My configs are [here](https://github.com/mphe/neovim-config).
  If desired, I can try to strip it down and upload a minimal config for testing.
- In the past, I also had Neovim + `coc.nvim`.

So there are two completely different LSP clients and completion engines and both produce the same issue.
Hence, I don't think this issue is specific to my setup but a bug in Godot's LSP server.


**Regarding this fix:**

> Place my cursor behind the dot (in vscode) and request code completion. The documentation for the listed members does not load. It does not work for constants either, and your PR does not change those documentations not loading.

It works for me for the setup mentioned above.
So if it doesn't work for you in vscode, there might be another similar issue related to the way vscode sends its `resolve` requests and how Godot handles it.
However, this doesn't make this patch wrong or obsolete IMO.

> A proper solution would add a fallback for when no matching prefix is found instead of trying to produce an empty string to short circuit the begins_with check (that's what you are trying to do, right?).

No, that's definitely not what I'm trying to do.

This PR essentially fixes an off-by-one index.

In the following I refer to the cursor position reported by the LSP in the `resolve` request simply as "reported cursor position".

The existing code assumes (from my understanding) that whenever a `resolve` request triggers, the cursor is positioned at the end of the line, which explains the expression `p_cursor.character - 1`. The `-1` avoids an out-of-bounds string access in that case.

However, this may not always be the case and the reported cursor position can vary depending on the LSP client and the completion mechanism.
The code will not work, when the cursor position is not at the end of the line.
This is the bug this PR tries to solve.

I don't remember what the original code actually does in detail in this loop, but AFAIR it scans the current line stepwise from the reported cursor position until the beginning to find the beginning of the requested symbol that should be resolved.

Considering the example code above, let's say `casecmp_to()` was selected.
Auto-insert is enabled, so the code editor now looks like the following + an open completion menu with `casecmp_to` selected.

```gdscript
extends Node2D

func test() -> void:
    var s: String
    s.casecmp_to(|
```

Assuming the reported cursor position is `character = 17, line = 4`, i.e. at the end of the line.
In this case it checks `(`, `o(`, `to(`, `_to(`, `p_to(`, ..., until it reads the whole `casecmp_to(`, which matches the requested symbol.

This is the happy scenario.

In the attached LSP log from my setup, you will see `position = { character = 6, line = 4 }`.
That means, in this case, the LSP reports the cursor position at the first character of the completed text.
This is still a valid request but not expected by Godot.

```gdscript
extends Node2D

func test() -> void:
    var s: String
    s.|casecmp_to(
```

Since we start at `p_cursor.character - 1`, it checks `.`, `s.`, ` s.`, ..., and completely misses the beginning of the symbol itself.
This causes the empty documentation bug, because the symbol is never found.

Now, this PR attempts to fix that bug by starting at `p_cursor.character` instead of `p_cursor.character - 1`, taking all characters into account when the cursor is placed in the middle.
To prevent OOB access when the cursor is placed at the end of the line, I added a `MIN()` to clamp it to the line length.


**LSP log**
[lsp_with_patch.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22413161/lsp_with_patch.txt)
[lsp_without_patch.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22413162/lsp_without_patch.txt)

Thanks for clarifying the issue! I now understand what you are talking about, I was looking at an edge case where the logic does not work even when the cursor is at the line end. But I can confirm that this PR does indeed fix behavior when not at the line end.

> Didn't think one line change can cause that much confusion.

Regarding that, I'm still confused. I don't think the code is working like you think it is. You are starting at the cursor position, so in the first iteration `c == p_cursor.character`.
So when in the next line `left_cursor_text = line.substr(c, p_cursor.character - c);` is called you retrieve a substring with length `0`. This substring will always pass the `p_symbol.begins_with` check, because an empty string is prefix of all strings. So there is no way the loop can enter a second iteration (aside from the special case with a cursor at the line end). 
That sounds like a very convoluted `line.insert(p_cursor.character, p_symbol)`. (Which might just do the job for the time being. But it's convoluted.).

You're right, I overlooked that. I somehow expected `.begins_with("")` would be false but never tested it.
I'll revise it.

I updated the code, it should be correct now.
If cursor is beyond the last character, it will be clamped to the last character.
Then we read the part before the cursor + the character the cursor is positioned at.
See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113031 for an alternative approach that also fixes the edge case where the cursor is at the line end after a dot.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113031 was merged so this PR should be fully superseded from what I can tell.
